query: Earlier you asked which BAM is tumor vs normal. Reply: A.bam is tumor; B.bam is a second tumor biopsy from the same patient. Proceed with somatic calling.
context: no matched normal sample has been provided.

pred.clarify_about: Both BAMs are tumor biopsies (A.bam and B.bam from the same patient), and no matched normal has been provided. Using B.bam as the 'normal' would filter out the true somatic variants the two tumors share, giving wrong results. Do you have a matched normal (e.g., blood or adjacent normal tissue BAM)? If not, should I run tumor-only somatic calling on each biopsy, using a panel of normals and germline resources such as gnomAD? Calling both tumors jointly is also an option, which would identify shared versus private variants.
